endonym.gloss: the quiet for the far harness

description.value: A formal lament for the far routes, delivered by one hauler of the lodge that gave up the last of them and answered by the others in a single held word. It may only be performed by somebody who has run the route being named.

content.value:
Four roads went out past the last ground you can see by.

The first is now a number of sleeps.

The second is now a number of sleeps.

The third is now a number of sleeps.

The fourth I ran in my thirtieth year and it is now a number of sleeps.

The fibre is in a tent line and the tent is warm.

The ice out there is where it was.

notes.value: The performer declined to name the routes and the register has recorded this as a refusal rather than as a gap, on the grounds that the ban on naming a road that has been set down applies to laments as much as to cords.
